summary.outcome_text: Accepted: the selected model passed the selection gate and all three test gates.

model_labels.reference: Zone and shot-type rates (reference, no gate)

definitions.target: Each field-goal attempt is made (1) or missed (0). Expected points = shot value (2 or 3) x make probability. Field-goal points only: free throws are not modelled, because a fouled missed shot is not a field-goal attempt and is absent from the shot data.
definitions.features: Before the shot only: location (x, y, distance, zone), shot value, the NBA's shot-type label (driving, pull-up, step-back, floating, dunk, putback and so on), period, seconds left in the period, score margin, seconds since the team gained possession (a transition proxy) and whether the possession had an offensive rebound. Never the shooter's identity and never whether the shot was assisted (the play-by-play records assists only on makes).
definitions.xpps: xPPS: expected points per shot, the mean expected value of the player's attempts. It describes the shots a player takes, not whether taking them is good.
definitions.pps: PPS: actual field-goal points per shot.
definitions.shot_making: Shot-making: 100 x ((PPS - xPPS) - league term), points per 100 shots above or below the expected value of the same shots, relative to the league in the same season. The league term is the league's PPS - xPPS in that season.
definitions.interval: Shot-making intervals: 95% bootstrap over the player's games (2,000 replicates). They show shot-outcome noise for a fixed model, not model error. Overlapping intervals do not rank two players.
definitions.metrics: Brier score: mean squared error of the make probability. Log loss: mean negative log likelihood. Lower is better for both. ECE: mean absolute gap between predicted and observed make rates over ten equal-width bins. Intervals are 95% game-bootstrap intervals (2,000 replicates).

reasons.small_sample: Fewer than 300 field-goal attempts in the season.

summary.credit: ShotQuality and the shot-quality / shot-making split are ShotQuality's and Databallr's concepts (databallr.com ShotQuality RAPM page, the design reference). CourtLens does not use the paid ShotQuality feed, which reads player tracking: this model reads free NBA shot and play-by-play data (via shufinskiy/nba_data), and its numbers are its own.
summary.reference_note: Design reference: a saved copy of Databallr's ShotQuality RAPM page (header, filters, ranked table in points per 100 shots, how-to-read and methodology panels). That page shows a RAPM decomposition (oTS, oSQ, oMake, oFT), which is Research block R06. It has no model card, calibration curve or per-player shot-making view, so those parts of this page have no reference.
summary.example_rule: Default player: the player with the most field-goal attempts in 2025-26 (a selection rule to open the page on a high-volume shooter, not a judgement of the player).
